questions.text: In Roman numerals, which letter stands for one thousand?
Which Roman emperor supposedly fiddled while Rome burned?
questions.explanation: Legend has Nero fiddling during the great fire of 64 AD.

questions.text: Which ancient Greek city-state was famed for its warriors?
questions.explanation: Sparta built its society around military training.

questions.text: In Greek myth, who ruled the sea?
questions.explanation: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea.

questions.text: What is the name of Rome's great amphitheatre where gladiators fought?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum was completed around 80 AD.

questions.text: Whose tomb did Howard Carter discover in 1922?
questions.explanation: Carter found the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.

questions.text: Who was the first emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Augustus became Rome's first emperor in 27 BC.

questions.text: In Greek myth, who flew too close to the sun on wings of wax?
questions.explanation: Icarus's wax wings melted and he fell into the sea.

questions.text: Which philosopher tutored Alexander the Great?
questions.explanation: Aristotle taught the young Alexander at the Macedonian court.

questions.text: Which Egyptian god, with the head of a jackal, is linked to mummification?
questions.explanation: Anubis was the jackal-headed god of embalming.

questions.text: Which 490 BC battle saw Athens defeat a Persian invasion force?
questions.explanation: The Athenian victory at Marathon halted Darius's first major invasion.

questions.text: Which Athenian statesman led the city in its golden age and championed the building of the Parthenon?
questions.explanation: Pericles dominated Athens in the fifth century BC and oversaw the Acropolis building programme.

questions.text: Which Roman general crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, sparking civil war?
questions.explanation: Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon began the civil war with Pompey.

questions.text: Which scholar deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs in the 1820s?
questions.explanation: Champollion used the Rosetta Stone to crack hieroglyphic writing in 1822.

questions.text: Which ancient wonder stood on the island of Pharos?
questions.explanation: The Pharos lighthouse guided ships into Alexandria's harbour.

spares.text: Which Greek goddess gave her name to the city of Athens?
spares.explanation: Athena was the patron goddess of Athens.

spares.text: Which Greek poet is traditionally credited with the Iliad?
spares.explanation: The Iliad is traditionally attributed to Homer.

spares.text: Which Roman emperor ordered a wall built across northern Britain from 122 AD?
spares.explanation: Hadrian's Wall began construction in 122 AD.
